title: Cable thieves strike again, target KSEB in Kasaragod twice in 48 hours
content: Kasaragod: Days after 11 members of a gang from Uttar Pradesh were arrested in connection with the theft of BSNL cables in Kannur and Thrissur, KSEB in Kasaragod has reported that its insulated cables and aluminium conductors were stolen from two sections 60 km apart within 48 hours. Police have not yet identified the culprits nor established whether the two thefts were connected. In the early hours of Thursday, six masked men stole two drums containing 1,000 metres of insulated aluminium cable worth around 4 lakh from Gunaje in Enmakaje panchayat, under the Perla KSEB Electrical Section. CCTV visuals show the men moving the heavy cable drums to load them onto a pickup vehicle. The latest theft came two days after a similar incident at Balanthode in Panathady panchayat, around 60 km from Perla. On September 22, masked men stole about 900 kg of old aluminium cables kept at the Balanthode KSEB section office after it was removed during line-replacement work. The material had only scrap value, said a KSEB official. The two incidents have several similarities. Both occurred around 2.30 am and involved masked men and a pickup vehicle. KSEB officials also said the vehicle seen in the Balanthode footage appeared similar to the one captured on camera at Perla. Perla Assistant Engineer Binu K V said he had submitted a complaint to Badiadka police station. According to the complaint, the theft came to light after a resident alerted the KSEB office by phone on Thursday morning. An inspection subsequently confirmed that the thieves stole two drums of low-tension aerial bunched (LT AB) cable meant for the Dyuthi power grid upgrade project. The CCTV footage shows six men with their faces covered arriving near the Gunaje transformer around 2.30 am. After hovering around for an hour, they managed to roll one of the heavy drums into the pickup using two poles as a makeshift ramp. "The footage shows the vehicle leaving with the first drum and returning about half an hour later to collect the second," Binu told Onmanorama. "We believe they travelled around 5km and shifted the drum to another vehicle before returning," he said. The pickup seen in the CCTV footage was registered in Kasaragod. "But we could see only KL 14 AE. The number was unclear in the footage," he said. The two drums were brought to Gunaje about two months ago to replace existing lines. Each drum contained 500 metres of insulated aluminium cable worth 2 lakh, Binu said. At Balanthode, meanwhile, the stolen material was old aluminium conductor recovered after an earlier line-replacement work. The material had been stored on the ground floor of the KSEB section office, while the office itself was on the first floor. Night-duty staff heard a noise around 2.30 am, but by the time they looked out, the men had fled after loading about 900 kg of conductor onto a pickup. There was no CCTV camera at the Balanthode section office, but footage from cameras along the route traced the pickup for about 35 km up to Bovikanam near Cherkala. The Rajapuram police have registered a case in connection with that theft. The incidents come shortly after police in Thrissur, Ernakulam and Kannur arrested 11 members of a Uttar Pradesh-based interstate gang pon charges of stealing copper cables. Police said the Meerut gang travelled to Kerala by air while their two-wheelers were transported by train. Police are examining whether other groups are involved in similar utility material thefts in the state.
